title: PlainActionFuture#assertCompleteAllowed false positives on concurrent resolve
description:
PlainActionFuture detects dangerous usage patterns where threads from the same pool are simultaneously resolving and waiting on the future. This is to prevent tests that deadlock and is only switched on when assertions are enabled.

This deadlock detection can falsely fire when threads from the same pool are simultaneously resolving a future.

The sequence of events is as follows:

T1 calls PlainActionFuture.Sync.complete with a value or exception, it successfully performs compareAndSet(RUNNING, COMPLETING) and proceeds to set the value/exception.
T2 calls PlainActionFuture.Sync.complete with a value or exception, if fails to perform compareAndSet(RUNNING, COMPLETING) while state is COMPLETING. It calls awaitShared to wait for T1 to finish.
T3 from the same pool as T2 attempts to complete the future, it throws in assertCompleteAllowed because there is a thread from the same pool (T2) waiting on the result.
This is a false-positive because T2 will definitely complete.

Note that T1 can be the same as T3 if completing the future in a loop or the thread gets recycled.

Steps to Reproduce
This has resulted in at least one test flake
